checklist: bash -c arithmetic
exec bash: $$ and $PPID unchanged, /proc/$$/stat shows bash
exec cat: /proc/$$/stat shows cat
exec cat /proc/self/stat: pid == $$ (slicc-kernel#108)
(exec sleep) &: child's $$ == $!, kill $! → wait 143
-O execfail: failed exec returns, USR1 trap restored
failed exec without execfail → 127

slicc-kernel#176 (shim-only proof on 1.26.6: shims/slicc/test/exec.test.mjs): exec readlink /proc/self == $$; 3-level exec bash chain keeps one pid; sh -c exec in a pipeline stage and a subshell exec keep that process's pid

/dev/tcp via the socket shim (netfork): realm-proxy round trip on 127.0.0.1:3128, $(hostname), refused port 'Connection refused', unknown host 'Name does not resolve', tailnet name dialled through the uplink (cert/net.mjs)

umask reaches the kernel (cert/umask.mjs, 5.3.0-10; slicc-kernel ≥ 1.35.1 kernelUmask): umask 077; : > f → 600 and /proc/self/status Umask 0077; umask 077; bash -c umask → 0077; umask 027 → touch 640, mkdir 750 (coreutils children); umask 077 → a WASIX child (perl open) creates 600; a subshell's umask does not leak back

pipes and close-on-exec (cert/pipes.mjs): (sleep 0.2; echo x) | cat ends; read + cat in a pipeline; a pipeline child holds 0 1 2 (+3, ls's own dirfd); exec 3>&1 → a child holds 0 1 2 3 (+4); seq 1 2000 through two cats

cert/writes.mjs (5.3.0-11): stdout reaches the kernel one write per flushed buffer, as on 5.3.0-7 (echo one -> ['one
'], printf 'a
b
' -> two line writes, 20 echos in a loop -> 20 writes, never a lone '
'); shims/slicc/slicc-writev.js gathers emscripten 4.0.23's per-iovec FS.write

cert/jobs.mjs (5.3.0-11, Killed since -12): in an interactive pty, ^C typed right after Enter interrupts the new job 20/20 (rc 130); ^Z stops it 20/20 ('Stopped'), and `kill -KILL %1` on each stopped job (no SIGCONT) is reported 'Killed' 20/20. Patches: jobs-parent-terminal.patch (the shell gives the terminal to a new foreground job too: the kernel-forked child takes it tens of ms late) and jobs-notify-unqueue.patch (notify_of_job_status reaps a SIGCHLD that arrives while it prints). Prompts are matched as '[$#] ': since 5.3.0-13 the kernel's default user is root, whose prompt ends in '#'

cert/users.mjs (5.3.0-13, H1 homescoop#207, slicc-kernel >= 1.44.0): ids, names and prompts from the kernel's process credentials (shims/slicc/slicc_libc_gaps.c over Module.sliccKernel.cred()). As root: UID=0 EUID=0 GROUPS=0 HOME=/root USER=root, PS1 \u \$ -> 'root #', ~ = /root, ~cone = /home/cone, a file written in ~ reads back; as kernel.users.add({name:'cone'}): UID=EUID=1000 GROUPS=1000 100 HOME=/home/cone USER=cone, 'cone $'; interactive bash --norc -i in a pty prompts '[root]# ' and '[cone]$ '. File owners are the kernel's (1.44.0 stores none, uid 1000) and not checked

cert/sigint-line.mjs (5.3.0-15, readline-sigint-discard.patch): (1) 20 fresh pty shells, 'sleep 0.1 && echo ranN' + Enter and ^C 0..19 ms later: never a partial command (5.3.0-13: 'leep'); (2) 20 rounds of 'true' + Enter, ^C 1..5 ms later, then 'echo nextN': every next line runs (5.3.0-14 dropped it: it freed the line that arrived after a late ^C). The patch tags each readline line with a sequence number; the SIGINT handler records the line it belongs to (the one readline is returning if accept-line already ran, else the earlier one) and how many characters readline held; shell_getc frees only that line, and a later line runs whole minus those characters. Certified on slicc-kernel 1.48.3 (has #303, released in 1.48.2); on kernel main 749ab1e 3/3 local runs pass; next-line phase alone, 40 rounds: -15 0 lost on main and on 1.47.1, -13 3 and 7

selfkill (5.3.0-18, slicc-kernel >= 1.73.2: #456, the kernel side of #422): bash -c 'kill -TERM $$' / -KILL / -INT ends bash by the signal: ctx.sync.run gives status null and signal 15/9/2, wait gives 128+n and the signal, nothing after the kill runs; 'exit 143' stays exit 143 with no signal; a trapped TERM prints its trap and bash goes on, an ignored one too. 5.3.0-17: every self-kill is a plain exit 128+n with no signal (slicc-kernel#422)

cert/ulimit.mjs (5.3.0-19, homescoop#178, shims/slicc/slicc_libc_gaps.c __syscall_prlimit64 + prlimit): as root and as kernel.users.add({name:'cone'}): ulimit -S -n / -H -n start at 4096 / 4096; ulimit -S -n 64 and ulimit -S -c 0 succeed and stick (64, 0); a subshell (fork) sees 64; ulimit -H -n 8192 fails 'cannot modify limit: Operation not permitted' (hard limits only go down, root too); ulimit -S -n 5000 over the hard limit fails 'Invalid argument'; ulimit -H -n 1024 succeeds, then ulimit -n 2048 fails EPERM; a new bash (exec) starts at 4096 again (slicc-kernel keeps no limits); ulimit -a shows open files 64 and core file size unlimited. 5.3.0-18: every change 'Operation not permitted' (NEGATIVE.md)

cert/symloop.mjs (5.3.0-19, scripts/emsdk-patches/libfs-symloop.patch, homescoop#611 / #461): bin/bash's FS.lookupPath has nlinks <= 40; bash's own redirections (echo hi >, read <) and [ -e ] work through chains of 39 and 40 symlinks, and the 41st follow is 'Symbolic link loop' (rc 1), as on Linux. 5.3.0-18: the 40-link redirect is ELOOP (NEGATIVE.md)

cert/siginherit.mjs (homescoop#973, shims/slicc/slicc_signals.c): a constructor seeds the sigaction table with SIG_IGN for each signal the kernel's sliccKernel.sigInherited() reports (bit n = signal n; only SIG_DFL entries, never SIGKILL/SIGSTOP, never a handler). On a kernel without the hook (the cert kernel today) the child of trap '' PIPE starts with defaults: bash -c 'trap -p PIPE' prints nothing, rc 0, no trap; a trap set in the same shell shows trap -- '' SIGPIPE. With the hook (slicc-kernel#967) the child prints trap -- '' SIGPIPE; that strict row comes with the kernel

cert/k122/siginherit.mjs (5.3.0-20, homescoop#973, on slicc-kernel 1.122.0): after trap '' PIPE, a child bash's trap -p shows exactly trap -- '' SIGPIPE (no TERM); a grandchild under trap '' PIPE INT shows both; an ignore set in a finished subshell is not inherited. 5.3.0-19's child shows nothing (NEGATIVE.md)

cert/fork-sigint.mjs (homescoop#1230, smoke row): a fresh interactive bash per round, its first forked job (sleep 5, sleep 5 | cat), ^C 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 60, 80, 120, 200 and 300 ms after Enter: bash is back at its prompt, runs echo after, and exits 0 (no exit 130, it keeps the terminal). Page-side timing can't land the ^C at proc-fork with the child's setpgid held, so this is a smoke row: 5.3.0-19 and -20 both pass it on slicc-kernel 1.73.2 and 1.125.4. The strict row with the NEGATIVE (-20 exits 130 before slicc-kernel#1146) waits for slicc-kernel/testing's fork hooks

test/fork-sigint.mjs (ci, homescoop#1230, slicc-kernel 1.130.2's setTestSyscallHook, users enforce, 3 rounds): an interactive bash in a terminal; at its first proc-fork the hook writes ^C, and the child's next proc-setpgid is held 300 ms; then echo "after": [child forked, bash still running, after printed] = [true, null, true]. A regression guard for slicc-kernel#1146's fix: 5.3.0-19 and -20 both pass on 1.130.2. On 1.129.0 (the hook, not the fix) 5.3.0-20 gives [true, 130, false] and -19 passes (NEGATIVE.md)
